summary: This Wikipedia-derived note covers the song "One Last Time" by Ariana Grande, from her second studio album "My Everything," and its music video. It describes the song's writers and producers, its promotional and single releases, and the French and Italian versions featuring Kendji Girac and Fedez. It also covers the found-footage music video, its cast including Matt Bennett and Elizabeth Gillies, and its view milestones.
one_line: Ariana Grande's 2014-2015 song "One Last Time" from the album "My Everything," with its found-footage music video and French and Italian versions.
key_facts: "One Last Time" was recorded by American singer Ariana Grande for her second studio album "My Everything".
The song was written by David Guetta, Savan Kotecha, Giorgio Tuinfort, Rami Yacoub, and Carl Falk.
"One Last Time" was first released on the iTunes Store on August 22, 2014, as the second promotional single from the album.
On February 10, 2015, the song was sent to contemporary hit radio as the fifth and final single from "My Everything".
A French version featuring Kendji Girac, alternatively titled "Attends-moi", was released on February 16, 2015 in France, Belgium and Switzerland.
The French version is also included on the deluxe version of Girac's debut studio album "Kendji" (2015).
An Italian version featuring Italian rapper Fedez was released on May 26, 2015 only in Italy.
The lyric video for "One Last Time" was released on Grande's official Vevo on February 6, 2015, the same day it was announced the music video was finished.
Grande released a teaser of the music video via Instagram on February 12, 2015, three days before the video's release.
The music video was released on Vevo on February 15, 2015, and was filmed in early January 2015.
The music video was visually presented as found footage, similar to Max Landis' previous work Chronicle.
Matt Bennett, Grande's co-star from the Nickelodeon sitcom Victorious, also stars in the music video.
Max Landis confirmed that actress Elizabeth Gillies, who also co-starred in Victorious, provided one of the voices of the news reporters at the beginning of the video.
Max Landis revealed "One Last Time" as Grande's next single after tweeting about the comet Eurydice.
The music video surpassed 100 million views on June 8, making it Grande's sixth Vevo-certified music video after "Love Me Harder".
